frequency_question: How often does structural friction (tooling transfer bottlenecks, intellectual property black-boxing, specialized material shortages, and precision machining dependencies) prevent successful domestic operationalization within a 2-to-3-year window?
membership_rule: Includes: major co-production or technology transfer initiatives for complex guided munitions or aerospace systems initiated under emergency/wartime constraints. Excludes: standard commercial licensing of small arms or assembly of purely non-critical components.

cases.name: India-Russia BrahMos supersonic cruise missile joint venture production
Pakistan Al-Khalid tank co-production with Chinese transfer
South Africa Project Cactus/Crotale missile domestic manufacturing attempt under arms embargo
Iran Hawk missile reverse engineering and domestic line (Project Sourena)
Argentina Condor II ballistic missile domestic production attempt
Ukraine Vilkha-M missile domestic production scaling attempt

coverage_note: 7 named; estimated universe of ~12 comparable severe-constraint missile localization attempts since 1950
known_gaps: Classified bilateral transfers between major powers during the Cold War where operational status lacks public verification.
skeleton: 7 major historical emergency guided-weapon/aerospace localization attempts matching structural transfer friction constraints
multiplier: 4 hits / 3 misses among identified comparable high-friction technology transfers
validity_reason: Industrial base globalization trends and digital manufacturing maturation change the friction baseline slowly over decades.
